bounds.domain: Two request IDs, three initial credit units, one- or two-unit reservation bounds, one account, and mutable plan/credential standing. Each request may have multiple sequential provider calls.
bounds.atomicity: The existing organization billing owner atomically reserves and settles funds. The Maps receipt owner rejects duplicate request keys before a second reservation. Settlement fixes its first known/unknown choice before a retryable attempt. An unknown choice conservatively charges the admitted bound; it is not a promise of a later refund.
bounds.progress: Weak fairness of finish(key) selects a terminal choice, and weak fairness of acknowledge(key) completes its retryable persistence. Permanent billing-owner failure is outside the progress premise.
bounds.composition: maps_request_buckets and maps_request_receipts cover the shared rate/receipt owner. This model covers the credit observation and liability boundary; it does not replace the organization billing owner.

limitations: Integer units abstract reservation bounds. Exact micro-USD arithmetic, minimum reservations, pricing buffers and ledger transaction implementation remain with the existing billing owner.

Observation is a classified billable provider result; a definite rejection releases only unused liability. Unclassified responses and lost later replies conservatively settle at the admitted estimate. The real-route and loopback HTTP cases check this classification boundary.
The finite state model is not universal TypeScript refinement. Authorization, database durability, cross-process transport and external invoice availability are separate owner contracts.
Google account-wide free caps and negotiated volume discounts require invoice reconciliation. Published unit quotes contain no platform markup.
A retry keeps the first settlement choice. Any later manual billing adjustment is outside this model; no automatic refund or invoice reconciliation is asserted.

assumptions: Weak fairness of finish(key) selects a known or unknown terminal choice. Weak fairness of acknowledge(key) assumes the billing owner eventually completes the same chosen settlement. Provider success and permanent storage availability are not proved.
Without scheduling and acknowledgment fairness, an admitted request or a selected settlement may wait forever.
